prompt: Promotions to a higher level should be made from within the company rather than appointing a new person from outside. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
When filling higher-level positions, companies can either promote existing staff or hire someone from outside. This essay completely agrees that promoting internal staff is better because it builds trust between management and workers while boosting overall productivity.

First, choosing managers from within the company strengthens relationships and trust across the workplace. When lower-level employees get promoted, they already understand the daily problems that regular staff face. Because they have worked their way up, these new managers know how to fix workplace issues quickly. This shared background builds strong loyalty and good communication between bosses and employees, which outside hires rarely achieve since they need months just to learn the company culture.

Second, promoting from within acts as a powerful motivation for other workers. When employees see a former co-worker earn a promotion through hard work, it proves to them that they also have a future at the company. This shows that effort is rewarded, encouraging everyone to work harder on their daily tasks. In contrast, constantly bringing in outside managers can make staff feel frustrated, signalling that loyalty will not help their careers grow.

In conclusion, companies should always prefer internal staff for promotions instead of hiring outside candidates. This approach builds strong trust across the company and keeps employees motivated to do their best work.
